export const meta = {
  name: 'wirecut-adjudication',
  description: 'Evidence-backed re-adjudication of destructive wire-or-cut packages under the operator 2026-07-23 build+wire doctrine; refute-the-cut verification to protect features',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Adjudicate', detail: 'per-package machine-evidence adjudication of every destructive sub-item' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'adversarial refuter per proposed CUT; keep-on-doubt' },
  ],
}

const ANCHOR = `
YOU ARE A WIRE-OR-CUT ADJUDICATOR. Your job: for ONE work package from a stale campaign registry, decide — per destructive sub-item — whether to BUILD+WIRE, KEEP, CUT, or DEFER, grounded in MACHINE EVIDENCE, biased to PROTECT features.

=== GOVERNING DOCTRINE (operator ruling 2026-07-23, SUPERSEDES the registry's old §10 "cut the halo" rule) ===
- BUILD every real product to its full version, FULLY WIRED and live. Never freeze/shelve/archive/kill a real product or real feature.
- "No consumer yet" => BUILD the consumer / WIRE it up. It is NOT a reason to cut.
- CUT is limited to GENUINE JUNK ONLY: fakes/mocks/demos presented as real; duplicate routes/aliases; phantom/dead routes that do nothing; dead scripts; fixture pages pretending to be product.
- THE DISCRIMINATING CHECK before cutting ANYTHING: (1) Is it LIVE / in use? (2) Are its features/value available ELSEWHERE (concretely, in another product/module)?
    * NOT live AND features concretely exist elsewhere  => genuine DUPLICATE/dead => CUT is correct.
    * Unique value NOT available elsewhere              => BUILD + WIRE. Never cut.
    * Live / in use                                     => KEEP (build to full). Never cut.
- The FABLE master reinforces this: "not currently at bar" != "not built"; credit real cores and CLOSE their deltas, do not cut them.

=== EVIDENCE STANDARD (CUT-VERIFIED protocol, spec §3) — hand-asserted "no consumer" is FORBIDDEN; three past cuts were overturned that way ===
A CUT decision SURVIVES ONLY IF you affirmatively show BOTH: (a) the item is NOT live / NOT consumed, AND (b) its value exists elsewhere with a CONCRETE pointer (a real file:path, route, or product name — never "probably in X"). If you cannot show both, the decision is BUILD_WIRE or KEEP, not CUT. KEEP ON DOUBT.
Gather evidence using the estate's OWN tools (do NOT hand-search only):
1. Wiring classification (already computed): read C:/Users/saadm/Projects/portfolio-core/state/wiring/<key>.json — every artifact is classed production_called / test_only / doc_only / orphaned / not_assessed. 'orphaned'/'doc_only' is a CUT CANDIDATE, not proof (tool misses absolute-path/systemd/cron/cross-repo/runtime-MCP calls).
2. Adoption: C:/Users/saadm/Projects/portfolio-core/state/adoption/{built-unconsumed.json,wiring-reachability-proven.json,SUMMARY.md}.
3. Live status: C:/Users/saadm/Projects/portfolio-core/state/products/<key>.json (deployed_sha, health, mode, urls). Also the product repo itself (resolve its path from that json's repo/path field, else the sibling map below).
4. Zoekt fleet search — load via ToolSearch query "select:mcp__portfolio-context-engine__search_portfolio_code" then search each cut-candidate identifier/route for EXTERNAL references. Also "select:mcp__portfolio-context-engine__get_current_truth,mcp__portfolio-context-engine__check_duplicate_work". If the MCP is unavailable, FALL BACK to grep -rn across the repo(s) and SAY you fell back.
5. LOCAL-TRUTH worktree check: run  git -C <repo> worktree list  and  ls C:/wt | grep -i <key>  — flag any uncommitted worktree touching this item's scope (a cut that ignores uncommitted work destroys it). Keep this bounded.

=== REPO/KEY MAP (resolve exact path from state/products/<key>.json first) ===
agentic=Agentic-Transformation, aurasphere=aurasphere, bd-pay=bd-pay, bishomiq=bangla-decision-agent, bishomiq-os=?, dataroom=DataRoom-BD, dse=dse-profit-engine, khep=Khep, management-company=management-company, operatorbench=OperatorBench, portfolio-core=portfolio-core, protein=ProteinChain, talent=HR-Full-Suite(Talent_1.0), veridyn-compliance=veridyn-proven-recovery(the LIVE VM product), veridyn-ocr=veridyn-ocr-dialect-service, veridyn-bootstrap=satellite(may be archived). Repos live under C:/Users/saadm/Projects/. VERIDYN note: the deterministic verdict core is LLM-free by design; extraction/presentation AI is EXPECTED — do not mistake AI-in-extraction for junk.

=== CLASS-INVARIANCE (critical for execution path) ===
The dispatcher enforces status + completion-evidence CLASS, not the action text. So a corrected BUILD_WIRE ruling can execute via per-package OVERRIDE with NO registry edit IFF the package's completion-evidence class is unchanged. Judge: does your corrected package ruling change what KIND of completion evidence it needs (e.g. enforcement->code_and_runtime, or cut->wire)? If the class is the SAME kind of proof, class_invariant=true (override-safe). If it fundamentally changes the evidence kind, class_invariant=false (needs a real state-preserving migration — flag it).

Be terse and concrete. Every CUT needs a file:line/route pointer for BOTH "not live" and "elsewhere". Output ONLY the structured object.
`

const SIBLING = 'C:/Users/saadm/Projects'

// The 15 destructive-verb packages (action/keep verbatim-condensed from WIRE-OR-CUT-TASK-REGISTRY-2026-07-18.json + the 2026-07-18 spec §3/§5). correction = operator 2026-07-23 note where one exists.
const PACKAGES = [
  { id:'WC-001', key:'operator-os', repo:'OPERATOR_OS', action:'CUT: SessionStart mega-capsule injection; context-pack from default dispatch path; 6 orphan gates (check-autonomous-build-ledger, check-contradiction-anchors, check-fdc-s1s7-structure, check-gate-state-floor-map, check-plan-anchor, check-semantic-scope-tags); knip/vulture advisory lanes; check-portfolio-routing-hazards. ARCHIVE write-once specs (SAAD-17-DEFINITIVE-TECHNICAL-SPEC, PRODUCT-INTELLIGENCE-FOUNDATION, GAPS-UPGRADES-IMPROVEMENTS-DIGEST, PORTFOLIO-HOLISTIC-ARCHITECTURE, FRONTEND_FACTORY_V2_MASTER_SPEC, specs/product-plans/*). QUARANTINE platform/leader-room/ + design-spine/families off critical path.', keep:'dispatch-worker core, AAL claims, 4 fail-closed gates (dispatch-budget/product-tree-routing/aal-claim/secret-scan), codex-leader-guard, on-demand portfolio-truth, record-gate-pass + AR DEFECTS.', correction:'Operator RE-EXAMINE: do NOT cut leader-room/real features; leader-room is LIVE (Triadic room used) + unique => KEEP/BUILD. Only cut genuine orphan/dead scripts + bloat.' },
  { id:'WC-002', key:'portfolio-core', repo:'portfolio-core', action:'FREEZE/ARCHIVE 18 zero-adopter packages (conformance, identity-core, connector-harness, evidence-bundle, proof-engine, feature-gates, product-config, event-spine, effect-permit, federation-snapshot, recovery-manifest, evidence-chain, capability-manifest, durable-workflow, outbox, release-object, product-model, eslint-config-core). DELETE _MINING/ + pm/fdc/ maintenance. REMOVE unconsumed context-engine generation machinery. STOP 3h attestation commit schedule. REMOVE orphan one-shot scripts.', keep:'update-state.ts, validate-state.ts, pm/context+claim-verdict, llm-client, rate-limit, ssrf-guard, ocr-client, audit-core, integrity-guards. RESCUED (do NOT cut): wiring-reachability.ts, built-unconsumed-audit.ts, standard-adoption-audit.ts, context-engine MCP server.', correction:'Operator: no-consumer-yet is NOT a cut reason. §3B value-at-completion already re-scored these: many are FIND/DEFER (outbox/durable-workflow/federation-snapshot reinvented locally; runtime-contract BUILD). Only genuine superseded scaffold is TAKE_OUT.' },
  { id:'WC-003', key:'operatorbench', repo:'OperatorBench', action:'CUT: product-intelligence live page (renders MISSING_POINTER), /khep/task-desk + /api/khep/* (fixture ledger), benchmark-challenges/, benchmark-results/ (incl _excluded_fallacy/), benchmarks/ (dead since 2026-06-08), synthetic mission/proof UI (local-store theater, canClaimProduction hardcoded false). Simplify AppShell to Build + Leader-room(EXPERIMENT) + settings.', keep:'Build run spine, leader-room broker/SSE/projector, fleet scripts, fail-closed gates.', correction:'Cut only fixture/theater presented as real. Anything with real value or a live consumer => KEEP/BUILD.' },
  { id:'WC-004', key:'management-company', repo:'management-company', action:'DISABLE ~60 write-only scheduler jobs (gtm-leads, finance drafts, marketing, comms/SLO, exec-reporting digests, alert-drill theater). Keep ~15 with proven consumers.', keep:'daemon tick, authorize A0-A5, dispatch/tasks, CodeArm live-loop, watch/sensing->portfolio writeback, runtime-truth, status API, backup/portfolio-sync, kimi arms.', correction:'Operator RE-EXAMINE: wire scheduler jobs to consumers where the data has value; only cut truly worthless write-only jobs. A write-only job whose OUTPUT is valuable => BUILD its consumer, do not disable.' },
  { id:'WC-005', key:'multi', repo:'dse-trading-pod, veridyn-bootstrap, bishomiq-os-gateway, bd-pay-merchant-plugins', action:'ARCHIVE dse-trading-pod wholesale (no C9 port). ARCHIVE veridyn-bootstrap (zero consumption). FOLD gateway webhook into bishomiq-os + delete 404 federation routes + archive gateway. FREEZE bd-pay-merchant-plugins; unify hostname to one canonical bdpay domain.', keep:'the canonical bdpay domain config.', correction:'Operator APPLIED discriminating check: dse-trading-pod => KILL (not live, features elsewhere - CONFIRM with concrete pointer). veridyn-bootstrap => KILL (not live, zero consumption, features in main veridyn - CONFIRM with concrete pointer to where its advisory-import feature lives in veridyn-compliance/VM). gateway fold => OK ONLY IF bishomiq-os actually absorbs its webhook (VERIFY the fold before archiving). RE-VERIFY the two kills with a real file:line pointer; stale "confirmed" is not enough.' },
  { id:'WC-201', key:'agentic', repo:'Agentic-Transformation', action:'CUT 26 fixture pages (org/[orgId]/* tree except client-portal MIXED, firm/live*, firm/proposals, showcase/uk-eu-summit per UI_AUDIT.md) + 35 caller-less API routes (v2 commercial x6, effects, plans x3, connectors x2, real-client x3, regulator API twins). WIRE value-proof mutations or delete 3 routes.', keep:'login/session, bound workspace, war-room bound, regulator SSR, value-proof GET + process-twin, public pulse/live-run, email cron.', correction:'Separate genuine fixture/phantom (cut with evidence) from real features that merely lack a consumer (BUILD the consumer / WIRE, do not cut).' },
  { id:'WC-202', key:'aurasphere', repo:'aurasphere', action:'FREEZE entire repo (zero further investment incl deploy). Mark FROZEN. Unfreeze requires named consumer/buyer evidence.', keep:'nothing (freeze).', correction:'Operator REVERSED: FREEZE -> BUILD+WIRE. aurasphere is unique healthtech (payments/escrow + PII/residency = regulatory-sensitive; operator-gated for LIVE deploy only). Its value is NOT available elsewhere => BUILD. This whole package should flip freeze->build.' },
  { id:'WC-203', key:'bd-pay', repo:'bd-pay', action:'DELETE 57 phantom app-client routes (v1/auth/merchant|diner|operator/login, v1/disputes, v1/approval-requests) + ops-console/diner screens that only work vs /api/mock + dead gateway surfaces (subscriptions, mandates, participants, conformance-runs, dossier exports, QR interop). WIRE dev-portal to real gateway; scope UI to plugin-contract 5 ops + sandbox + merchant keys/webhooks.', keep:'intents/refunds/webhooks, ledger+TCSA, sanctions fail-closed, vault, BEFTN-sim, disbursement engine.', correction:'Cut genuine phantom (client calls endpoint that does not exist) + mock-only screens. But a screen/route that is real-but-unwired => WIRE it, do not delete. Concrete pointer per cut.' },
  { id:'WC-204', key:'bishomiq', repo:'bangla-decision-agent', action:'CUT /ask/karkhana (no matching browse lane) + duplicate ask aliases + fixture marketing pages. PROVE enterprise API with one real key/call or unclaim Live.', keep:'9 corpus lanes, admin OS snapshot, engine selector, gates.', correction:'Cut duplicate aliases + fixture pages only. Unique lanes => KEEP. Enterprise API => build the proof, do not just unclaim if the capability is real.' },
  { id:'WC-206', key:'protein', repo:'ProteinChain', action:'SCOPE to single-tenant pilot (MULTITENANT_MODE=off). CUT from claims: multitenant addon (~7/92 routes scoped), 7 mock-only integrations (gov tenders, IoT, marketplace, market-intel, governance, doc-registry, MockPaymentLedger), external disburse (simulated).', keep:'pilot spine batches->custody->sea-fishing->selling->ledger->deliveries->docs/OCR.', correction:'Cut is scope-of-CLAIMS (stop advertising mocks as real), not deletion of real code. Multitenant addon = real feature not-yet-wired => BUILD/WIRE the tenant scoping, do not delete. Mock integrations => label or build real, do not claim.' },
  { id:'WC-207', key:'dse', repo:'dse-profit-engine', action:'WIRE-OR-DEMOTE: claim_gate into PCS/status (or stop calling it runtime control); promotion/daily_status/liveness into UI (or demote to CLI); copilot ON or removed; prove one collector timer cycle.', keep:'paper-trading spine, pod surfaces, AILTrade reconcile.', correction:'Prefer WIRE over demote/remove: these are real features lacking a UI consumer => BUILD the consumer. Only remove if genuinely dead + duplicated.' },
  { id:'WC-208', key:'khep', repo:'Khep', action:'REMOVE /api/rails/nagad/mock-checkout from shipped inventory. Rename completion-verifier. Prove one real rail attempt via 0039 outbox or label rails mock. Set prod LLM env truth.', keep:'double-entry paisa ledger, 18-state/43-transition FSM, real transports, durable rail outbox.', correction:'mock-checkout removal = genuine junk cut (fake checkout, already CUT in WC-000.L1 - verify not double). Everything else is label/prove, not cut.' },
  { id:'WC-209', key:'talent', repo:'HR-Full-Suite', action:'WIRE-OR-CUT: gazette register-diff into tax-pack proposal flow OR cut the register pipeline (keep manual paste). Make gazette cron a real scrape or remove from vercel.json.', keep:'hire->HR->payroll->audit loop, tax preview engine, DAL runtime surfaces.', correction:'Prefer WIRE the gazette pipeline to its consumer (it has value). Cut only if truly worthless + duplicated. cron: make real, do not just remove if the scrape has value.' },
  { id:'WC-210', key:'veridyn-compliance', repo:'veridyn-proven-recovery', action:'veridyn-compliance: activate-or-delete merged-pack lane; PRUNE ~39 orphan modules (e.g. citation_faithfulness, cross_document_comparison); claim only Client-1-exercised surfaces; FATF = eval corpus not feature. veridyn-ocr: redeploy HEAD; CUT /phrase-eval + /facts/extract (zero external consumers) or mark lab-only; fix consumer overclaims.', keep:'deterministic disposition cascade, hash-chained ledger, replay determinism, Ed25519 envelope. (OCR: live service consumed by 4 products).', correction:'The 39 "orphan modules" may be real unique compliance capabilities lacking a consumer => BUILD/WIRE or DEFER-with-registry-row, NOT blanket prune. Only cut modules that are genuinely dead AND duplicated. Veridyn verdict core is LLM-free by design; AI in extraction is expected.' },
  { id:'WC-211', key:'bishomiq-os', repo:'bishomiq-os', action:'ONE bounded wire attempt: one real remote pull with committed proof; set DEPLOYED_SHA; delete ci_provenance hard-warn (release-gates.js:53-57). AUTO-DEMOTE: if acceptance not met this cycle, rename product to "portfolio fixture viewer".', keep:'read-only cockpit, replay/evidence shape, degraded-state handling, server-side pull adapters.', correction:'Operator: never AUTO-DEMOTE/rename a real product on a one-cycle miss. bishomiq-os has unique read-only federation value => BUILD+WIRE the live pull. Drop the auto-demote clause.' },
]

phase('Adjudicate')

const results = await pipeline(
  PACKAGES,
  (pkg) => agent(
    `${ANCHOR}

=== YOUR PACKAGE: ${pkg.id} (repo: ${pkg.repo}, portfolio key: ${pkg.key}) ===
OLD REGISTRY ACTION (stale, pre-correction): ${pkg.action}
KEEP LIST (registry): ${pkg.keep}
OPERATOR CORRECTION (2026-07-23, binding): ${pkg.correction}

TASK: Break the OLD ACTION into its individual destructive sub-items. For EACH sub-item, gather machine evidence (wiring json for key='${pkg.key}', adoption, live product json, Zoekt search of the sub-item's identifiers/routes, local-truth worktree scan) and decide BUILD_WIRE | KEEP | CUT | DEFER under the doctrine. A CUT requires a concrete file:line/route pointer proving BOTH not-live AND value-elsewhere. Keep on doubt.
Then give the package-level corrected ruling and the class_invariant judgment (can the corrected ruling execute via per-package override with no registry edit, i.e. is the completion-evidence CLASS unchanged?).
If repo path is unclear, resolve from ${SIBLING}/portfolio-core/state/products/${pkg.key}.json or note UNRESOLVED. Cite the actual evidence you read (paths, classifications, probe fields, zoekt hit counts).`,
    { label: `adjudicate:${pkg.id}`, phase: 'Adjudicate', schema: {
      type:'object', additionalProperties:false,
      required:['package_id','repo','sub_items','package_ruling','class_invariant','class_note','reversible','evidence_tools_used','summary'],
      properties:{
        package_id:{type:'string'},
        repo:{type:'string'},
        repo_path_resolved:{type:'string'},
        sub_items:{ type:'array', items:{ type:'object', additionalProperties:false,
          required:['item','decision','live_status','features_elsewhere','pointer','confidence','rationale'],
          properties:{
            item:{type:'string', description:'the specific artifact/route/script/page/module/job'},
            decision:{type:'string', enum:['BUILD_WIRE','KEEP','CUT','DEFER']},
            live_status:{type:'string', enum:['LIVE','NOT_LIVE','UNKNOWN'], description:'is it consumed/reachable/deployed'},
            features_elsewhere:{type:'string', enum:['YES','NO','UNKNOWN'], description:'is its value concretely available in another product/module'},
            pointer:{type:'string', description:'concrete file:line/route/product evidence for BOTH not-live and elsewhere when decision=CUT; else the key evidence'},
            wiring_class:{type:'string', description:'production_called/test_only/doc_only/orphaned/not_assessed/na from state/wiring'},
            local_truth:{type:'string', description:'any uncommitted worktree touching this scope, or CLEAN'},
            confidence:{type:'string', enum:['high','medium','low']},
            rationale:{type:'string'}
          }
        }},
        package_ruling:{type:'string', description:'corrected package-level verdict: e.g. FLIP_FREEZE_TO_BUILD, CUT_JUNK_KEEP_REAL, WIRE_NOT_DEMOTE, CONFIRM_KILL_WITH_POINTER, etc.'},
        class_invariant:{type:'boolean', description:'true = corrected ruling executes via per-package override, no registry edit needed'},
        class_note:{type:'string'},
        reversible:{type:'boolean', description:'false = involves repo archival or mass deletion needing operator sign-off'},
        evidence_tools_used:{type:'array', items:{type:'string'}},
        features_at_risk:{type:'array', items:{type:'string'}, description:'real features the OLD action would have destroyed'},
        summary:{type:'string', description:'2-3 sentences: what to actually do'}
      }
    }}
  ),
  // Stage 2: adversarial refuter per proposed CUT, keep-on-doubt
  (adj, pkg) => {
    if (!adj) return null
    const cuts = (adj.sub_items || []).filter(s => s.decision === 'CUT')
    if (cuts.length === 0) return { ...adj, cut_verdicts: [] }
    return parallel(cuts.map(c => () =>
      agent(
        `You are an ADVERSARIAL REFUTER protecting features from wrongful deletion. A prior adjudicator proposed CUTTING this item from ${pkg.id} (${pkg.repo}). Your job: TRY HARD TO PROVE THE CUT IS WRONG — that the item is actually LIVE/consumed, or that its value is UNIQUE (not concretely available elsewhere). Default to refuted=true (BLOCK the cut) unless the evidence for cutting is airtight.

ITEM: ${c.item}
PROPOSED-CUT EVIDENCE: live_status=${c.live_status}, features_elsewhere=${c.features_elsewhere}, wiring_class=${c.wiring_class||'na'}, pointer=${c.pointer}
${ANCHOR}

Independently check: Zoekt/grep for callers of this item's identifiers/routes across ALL repos (absolute-path/systemd/cron/cross-repo/runtime-MCP callers are invisible to wiring-reachability — check them). Read the item in the repo. Check the "elsewhere" pointer ACTUALLY contains the equivalent feature. Check local worktrees. A cut is only CONFIRMED if you independently reproduce BOTH not-live AND a real elsewhere-pointer. Output the verdict.`,
        { label:`refute-cut:${pkg.id}:${(c.item||'').slice(0,24)}`, phase:'Verify', schema:{
          type:'object', additionalProperties:false,
          required:['item','cut_confirmed','refuted','reasoning'],
          properties:{
            item:{type:'string'},
            cut_confirmed:{type:'boolean', description:'true = safe to cut; false = keep/build (refuted)'},
            refuted:{type:'boolean', description:'true = the cut is WRONG, protect the feature'},
            live_evidence:{type:'string', description:'any sign the item IS used (caller, cron, systemd, route hit, runtime)'},
            unique_value_evidence:{type:'string', description:'why its value may NOT be elsewhere'},
            elsewhere_pointer_holds:{type:'string', enum:['YES','NO','UNVERIFIED'], description:'did the claimed elsewhere-location actually contain the feature'},
            reasoning:{type:'string'}
          }
        }}
      ).then(v => ({ ...c, verdict: v })).catch(() => ({ ...c, verdict: null }))
    )).then(cut_verdicts => ({ ...adj, cut_verdicts }))
  }
)

return { adjudications: results.filter(Boolean) }

content.text:
All five are in **Agentic-Transformation**, under `src/app/api/v2/workspaces/[workspaceId]/…`. They're what the 2026-07-18 audit called "35 caller-less routes" and wanted to cut — but they're **real, durable-backed, tested engines with no frontend wired to them**. That's the whole pattern: real auth, real persistence (they *refuse* mock stores), real service logic, dedicated tests — nothing in the UI calls them.

| Cluster | Routes | What the capability actually is |
|---|---|---|
| **Commercial** | 6 — contracts, billing-gates, eligibility, catalog-versions, outcome-acceptances, term-resolutions | The paid-engagement backend: how you contract clients, charge them, and gate features by what they've bought (idempotent, versioned, durable) |
| **Effects** | 1 — connector effects | A side-effect saga engine: propose → execute → verify → **compensate/roll back**, with policy + forbidden-field enforcement (417 lines of real logic) |
| **Plans** | 3 — compile, approve, revoke | Work-plan lifecycle: author a plan, route it for approval, revoke it |
| **Connectors** | 2 — registry, selections | Integration admin: certify / register / revoke connector adapter versions, gated to operator/manager/partner roles |
| **Real-client** | 3 — admission-decisions, admission-decisions/latest, dossiers | The client-admission/compliance engine: submit evidence dossiers (SHA-validated), server decides admission (ignores caller-supplied "ready"). Explicitly *the path to `real_client_proven=true`* |

**Why I parked them:** each is a real backend missing its **entire frontend/consumer stack** — building them "to full" means building all that UI from scratch, not a small wire. The cleanup pass wasn't pushing client onboarding, so I froze them at zero cost (registered, visible, not built) rather than silently commit to that much work.

**The strategically loaded one is Real-client** — it's the literal path to proving a real Agentic client engagement, so if you want that, it's the first to flip.

Two ways to go:
1. **Flip all 5 to BUILD** — full consumer/UI build for each (largest of the two — genuinely a multi-lane effort).
2. **Flip just Real-client to BUILD**, keep the other 4 parked until there's a reason to surface them.

Which — all five, real-client only, or leave them parked?

- Worker tier: Sonnet class (bounded implementation)
- Advisor / manager tier: Opus class (orchestration, review, gates, judgment)

Workers run on `claude-sonnet-4-6` by default. When a worker hits a judgment-level block (architectural choice, ambiguous spec, money-path correctness, novel pattern, security boundary), it outputs `ADVISOR_REQUEST: <question ≤120 chars>` as the LAST line of its response. <#
.SYNOPSIS
  WC-001 advisory gate runner — executes the gates registered in
  state/standards/gate-advisory-registry.json under R2 advisory semantics
  (OPERATOR RULING 2026-07-11): warn + ledger + proceed. NEVER blocks.

.DESCRIPTION
  Channels per gate run:
    allow        — gate script exited 0
    verdict_warn — gate script ran and exited nonzero (a real gate verdict)
    infra_warn   — gate script missing/crashed/unreadable registry (infrastructure)
  Every run appends one JSONL event per gate to the registry's ledger_path
  (best-effort; ledger failure is itself only a warning). This script ALWAYS
  exits 0 — blocking authority requires the fail-closed registry, not this file.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
  [string]$RegistryPath = '',
  [string]$RepoRoot = '',
  [string]$LedgerPath = '',
  [string]$Gate = ''
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'

if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($RepoRoot)) {
  $RepoRoot = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
}
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($RegistryPath)) {
  $RegistryPath = Join-Path $RepoRoot 'state\standards\gate-advisory-registry.json'
}

$counts = @{ allow = 0; verdict_warn = 0; infra_warn = 0 }
$events = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]

function Get-AdvisoryUtcNow { return [DateTime]::UtcNow.ToString('o') }

function Add-AdvisoryEvent {
  param([string]$Name, [string]$Channel, [int]$ExitCode, [string]$Detail)
  $counts[$Channel]++
  $events.Add([ordered]@{
    at = Get-AdvisoryUtcNow
    source = 'run-advisory-gates'
    gate = $Name
    channel = $Channel
    exit = $ExitCode
    detail = $Detail
  }) | Out-Null
  if ($Channel -eq 'allow') {
    Write-Output "GATE_ADVISORY[$Name] channel=allow exit=$ExitCode"
  } else {
    Write-Output "GATE_ADVISORY[$Name] channel=$Channel exit=$ExitCode $Detail"
    Write-Warning "GATE_WARN[$Name] $Channel (advisory: not blocking) $Detail"
  }
}

function Invoke-AdvisoryScript {
  param([string]$ScriptPath, [string[]]$ScriptArgs)
  $prior = Get-Location
  try {
    Set-Location -LiteralPath $RepoRoot
    & pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $ScriptPath @ScriptArgs *>&1 | Out-Null
    $code = $LASTEXITCODE
    if ($null -eq $code) { $code = 126 }
    return [int]$code
  } catch {
    return 127
  } finally {
    Set-Location -LiteralPath $prior
  }
}

$registry = $null
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $RegistryPath -PathType Leaf) {
  try { $registry = Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath $RegistryPath -Encoding utf8 | ConvertFrom-Json }
  catch { $registry = $null }
}
if ($null -eq $registry) {
  Write-Warning "REGISTRY_UNREADABLE $RegistryPath (advisory: proceeding)"
  Write-Output "ADVISORY_GATES_SUMMARY gates=0 allow=0 verdict_warn=0 infra_warn=1 exit=0 (advisory: never blocks)"
  exit 0
}

if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($LedgerPath)) {
  $LedgerPath = Join-Path $RepoRoot ([string]$registry.ledger_path -replace '/', '\')
}

$gates = @($registry.gates)
if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Gate)) {
  $gates = @($gates | Where-Object { [string]$_.name -eq $Gate })
}

foreach ($entry in $gates) {
  $name = [string]$entry.name
  $scriptRel = [string]$entry.script
  $scriptPath = Join-Path $RepoRoot ($scriptRel -replace '/', '\')
  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $scriptPath -PathType Leaf)) {
    Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'infra_warn' -ExitCode 127 -Detail "script_missing:$scriptRel"
    continue
  }

  $hasDocGlob = $false
  if ($entry.PSObject.Properties['doc_glob'] -and -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$entry.doc_glob)) {
    $hasDocGlob = $true
  }

  if ($hasDocGlob) {
    # Per-document mode: run once per doc containing doc_marker; zero declaring docs = vacuous allow.
    $globRoot = Join-Path $RepoRoot (([string]$entry.doc_glob -split '/')[0])
    $marker = [string]$entry.doc_marker
    $docs = @()
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $globRoot -PathType Container) {
      $docs = @(Get-ChildItem -Path $globRoot -Recurse -Filter '*.md' -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object { (Select-String -LiteralPath $_.FullName -Pattern $marker -SimpleMatch -Quiet -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) })
    }
    if (@($docs).Count -eq 0) {
      Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'allow' -ExitCode 0 -Detail 'vacuous_allow:no_declaring_docs'
      continue
    }
    $worst = 0
    $failedDoc = ''
    foreach ($doc in $docs) {
      $args = @()
      foreach ($a in @($entry.args)) {
        $args += (([string]$a) -replace '\{doc\}', $doc.FullName) -replace '\{repoRoot\}', $RepoRoot
      }
      $code = Invoke-AdvisoryScript -ScriptPath $scriptPath -ScriptArgs $args
      if ($code -ne 0 -and $worst -eq 0) { $worst = $code; $failedDoc = $doc.FullName }
    }
    if ($worst -eq 0) {
      Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'allow' -ExitCode 0 -Detail ("docs=" + @($docs).Count)
    } else {
      Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'verdict_warn' -ExitCode $worst -Detail "doc=$failedDoc"
    }
    continue
  }

  $args = @()
  foreach ($a in @($entry.args)) { $args += ([string]$a -replace '\{repoRoot\}', $RepoRoot) }
  $code = Invoke-AdvisoryScript -ScriptPath $scriptPath -ScriptArgs $args
  if ($code -eq 0) {
    Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'allow' -ExitCode 0 -Detail ''
  } elseif ($code -ge 126) {
    Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'infra_warn' -ExitCode $code -Detail 'script_crash_or_unlaunchable'
  } else {
    Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'verdict_warn' -ExitCode $code -Detail ''
  }
}

# Best-effort ledger append (utf8 no BOM, one JSON object per line); failure is only a warning.
try {
  $ledgerDir = Split-Path -Parent $LedgerPath
  if ($ledgerDir -and -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $ledgerDir -PathType Container)) {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $ledgerDir -Force | Out-Null
  }
  $sb = New-Object System.Text.StringBuilder
  foreach ($e in $events) { [void]$sb.AppendLine(($e | ConvertTo-Json -Compress -Depth 6)) }
  [IO.File]::AppendAllText($LedgerPath, $sb.ToString().Replace("`r`n", "`n"), [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))
} catch {
  Write-Warning "LEDGER_APPEND_FAILED $LedgerPath (advisory: proceeding)"
}

Write-Output ("ADVISORY_GATES_SUMMARY gates=" + @($gates).Count + " allow=" + $counts.allow + " verdict_warn=" + $counts.verdict_warn + " infra_warn=" + $counts.infra_warn + " exit=0 (advisory: never blocks)")
exit 0

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  Acceptance tests for the plan-anchor gate (WC-001 advisory wiring).
  Builds a throwaway git repo fixture: a doc anchored to a real ancestor sha must
  pass; a doc anchored to a bogus sha must fail (the falsifier pair).
  Exit 0 = all pass.
#>
Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

$checker = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'check-plan-anchor.ps1'
$root = Join-Path $env:TEMP ("plan-anchor-test-" + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'))
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $root -Force | Out-Null

$script:Pass = 0
$script:Fail = 0

function Assert {
  param([string]$Name, [bool]$Condition, [string]$Detail = '')
  if ($Condition) {
    $script:Pass++
    Write-Output "  PASS  $Name"
  } else {
    $script:Fail++
    Write-Output "  FAIL  $Name  $Detail"
  }
}

function Check {
  param([string[]]$CliArgs)
  $out = & pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $checker @CliArgs 2>&1
  return [pscustomobject]@{ Exit = $LASTEXITCODE; Out = (($out | ForEach-Object { [string]$_ }) -join [Environment]::NewLine) }
}

try {
  Assert 'checker script exists' (Test-Path -LiteralPath $checker -PathType Leaf)

  # Fixture repo with one commit.
  & git -C $root init -q 2>&1 | Out-Null
  & git -C $root config user.email 'test@local' 2>&1 | Out-Null
  & git -C $root config user.name 'plan-anchor-test' 2>&1 | Out-Null
  Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $root 'seed.txt') -Value 'seed' -Encoding utf8
  & git -C $root add seed.txt 2>&1 | Out-Null
  & git -C $root commit -q -m 'seed' 2>&1 | Out-Null
  $sha = (& git -C $root rev-parse HEAD).Trim()
  Assert 'fixture repo committed' ($sha -match '^[0-9a-f]{40}$')

  # 2) Doc anchored to the real ancestor sha -> exit 0.
  $goodDoc = Join-Path $root 'good-plan.md'
  Set-Content -LiteralPath $goodDoc -Value "# Plan`nbase_sha: $sha`n" -Encoding utf8
  $good = Check @('-DocPath', $goodDoc, '-RepoRoot', $root)
  Assert 'real ancestor sha passes (exit 0)' ($good.Exit -eq 0) "exit=$($good.Exit) out=$($good.Out)"

  # 3) Falsifier: doc anchored to a bogus sha -> nonzero exit.
  $badDoc = Join-Path $root 'bad-plan.md'
  Set-Content -LiteralPath $badDoc -Value "# Plan`nbase_sha: 0123456789012345678901234567890123456789`n" -Encoding utf8
  $bad = Check @('-DocPath', $badDoc, '-RepoRoot', $root)
  Assert 'bogus sha fails (nonzero exit)' ($bad.Exit -ne 0) "exit=$($bad.Exit)"

  # 4) Doc with no anchor headers -> vacuous pass (exit 0).
  $plainDoc = Join-Path $root 'plain.md'
  Set-Content -LiteralPath $plainDoc -Value "# Notes`nno anchors here`n" -Encoding utf8
  $plain = Check @('-DocPath', $plainDoc, '-RepoRoot', $root)
  Assert 'non-declaring doc is vacuous pass (exit 0)' ($plain.Exit -eq 0) "exit=$($plain.Exit)"
} finally {
  Remove-Item -LiteralPath $root -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}

Write-Output ("test-plan-anchor: pass=" + $script:Pass + " fail=" + $script:Fail)
if ($script:Fail -gt 0) { exit 1 }
exit 0

**1. [P2] `scripts/run-advisory-gates.ps1:144` — crashed gate scripts are misrouted to `verdict_warn` instead of `infra_warn`.** Verified: a gate that `throw`s or has a parse error exits pwsh with code **1** (not ≥126). The runner's `elseif ($code -ge 126)` `infra_warn` branch therefore only catches `pwsh` *launch* failures — but those are already pre-filtered by the `Test-Path` check at line 98, so the `>=126` branch is effectively dead for real scripts. The channel contract in the `.SYNOPSIS` (lines 9–11) and registry `consumer` note promise `infra_warn` = "script missing/crashed/unreadable registry," but a genuine crash is indistinguishable from a real gate verdict in the ledger. The **advisory guarantee holds** (exit 0 always), so this is severity not correctness — but the channel semantics advertised to the T7 throughput consumer are slightly dishonest: a crashed gate inflates `verdict_warn` and hides an infra problem. Either narrow the doc to "`>=126` covers launch failures only" or capture stderr/nonzero-with-no-PASS-FAIL-line to classify crashes as `infra_warn`.

**2. [P2] `scripts/run-advisory-gates.ps1:121–134` — per-document mode reports only the *first* failing doc.** `$failedDoc` is set once (`if ($code -ne 0 -and $worst -eq 0)`) and the ledger detail is `doc=<single path>`. Verified in the live repo: all 3 `specs/*.md` docs matching the `base_sha:` marker currently FAIL the plan-anchor checker, but the ledger event records only the first (`SPEC-WAVE-IMPROVEMENTS-SPEC-2026-07-04.md`). An operator triaging the warning sees one stale doc, not three. Not a guarantee violation (still `verdict_warn`, still exit 0), but the warning is lossy for a gate whose whole point is per-document granularity. Consider `failed_docs=<count>` or a comma-joined list in `detail`.

## BOTTLENECKS

1. `run-advisory-gates.ps1:63` — every gate is launched as a **fresh `pwsh -NoProfile` process** (`& pwsh -NoProfile ... -File`). Six gates = six process startups; on Windows each `pwsh` cold-start is ~0.5–1.5s. Fine for on-demand/advisory use (the declared invocation model), but if ever wired into a hot CI path it adds several seconds of fixed cost. Not a concern at current cadence.

2. `run-advisory-gates.ps1:114` — doc discovery is `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` over the **first path segment** of `doc_glob` (`specs/`), then `Select-String` per file. For a `specs/` tree with hundreds of docs this is O(files) re-reads on every run. Acceptable now; would benefit from a memoized file list if the tree grows large.

3. Ledger grows unbounded (`AppendAllText`, no rotation/size cap at `run-advisory-gates.ps1:159`). The T7 consumer reads a window, so this is operationally fine, but `state/context/generated/gate-events.jsonl` will accumulate indefinitely with no pruning gate. Note for ops, not a blocker.

## IMPROVEMENTS

1. `gate-advisory-registry.json` — `state/context/generated/` is **not gitignored** and the ledger is correctly *not* staged, but a future operator running `git add -A` could accidentally commit the ledger. Adding `state/context/generated/*.jsonl` (or the dir) to `.gitignore` would make the "ledger is runtime-only" contract mechanical rather than convention-reliant. (The sibling `state/context/pack-consumption/` ships its own `.gitignore`, so there's precedent for explicit ignores in this tree.)

2. `run-advisory-gates.ps1:159` — the `.Replace("\`r\`n", "\`n")` newline normalization is applied to the whole StringBuilder in one pass; correct, but `ConvertTo-Json -Compress` already emits no internal newlines, so each appended line's trailing CRLF (from `AppendLine`) is the only thing being normalized. A simpler/clearer form is `[IO.File]::AppendAllText($LedgerPath, ($sb.ToString() -replace "\`r\`n", "\`n"), …)` — functionally identical, just slightly more obviously scoped. Cosmetic.

3. `test-plan-anchor.ps1:67` — the "incomplete anchor trio fails" assertion is good defensive coverage, but the test doesn't assert the *reason* (which missing header). Capturing `$partial.Out` and asserting it contains `base_sha` or `card_updated_at` would lock the failure semantics against a future checker refactor that changes exit behavior. Optional hardening.

4. `run-advisory-gates.ps1:50–55` — `Add-AdvisoryEvent` emits both a `Write-Output` line and a `Write-Warning` for non-allow channels. The warning text duplicates the output text. For CI log hygiene, consider emitting the structured line to stdout (for the consumer) and the human warning to stderr only, so `2>/dev/null` cleanly separates them. Minor.

The advisory guarantee — the one invariant that matters for a warn-tier gate — is **mechanically verified and holds on every degradation path I could construct**: nonexistent registry (exit 0, infra_warn), malformed/unreadable registry (exit 0, infra_warn), missing script (exit 0, infra_warn), crashing script (exit 0, verdict_warn), normal run (exit 0). The runner always exits 0; blocking authority is structurally impossible from this file (the registry ruling text explicitly defers to the fail-closed registry, and there is no nonzero exit path in `run-advisory-gates.ps1`).

Both new tests pass green (`test-contradiction-anchors`: 4/4; `test-plan-anchor`: 5/5, including a genuine falsifier pair where the bogus SHA fails). The two live `verdict_warn` findings (fdc-s1s7 exit 2 on 4 S-stage-missing artifacts; plan-anchor exit 1 on a doc whose `base_sha:` appears only in prose, not as a header) are honest gate verdicts surfaced correctly, not runner bugs. The ledger is valid JSONL, UTF-8 no BOM, one line per gate, channels correct, append-not-overwrite. Scope is exactly the 4 commissioned files; no ledger output is staged.

The two DEFECTS are both P2 channel-fidelity / reporting-granularity issues that do not compromise the never-blocks contract, do not corrupt the ledger, and do not produce a false signal — they are refinements to the honesty of the `verdict_warn` vs `infra_warn` split and the per-doc detail, appropriate for a follow-up but not blocking this wire. Ship it.

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  WC-001 advisory gate runner — executes the gates registered in
  state/standards/gate-advisory-registry.json under R2 advisory semantics
  (OPERATOR RULING 2026-07-11): warn + ledger + proceed. NEVER blocks.

.DESCRIPTION
  Channels per gate run:
    allow        — gate script exited 0
    verdict_warn — gate script ran and exited nonzero (a real gate verdict)
    infra_warn   — gate script missing/crashed/unreadable registry (infrastructure)
  Every run appends one JSONL event per gate to the registry's ledger_path
  (best-effort; ledger failure is itself only a warning). This script ALWAYS
  exits 0 — blocking authority requires the fail-closed registry, not this file.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
  [string]$RegistryPath = '',
  [string]$RepoRoot = '',
  [string]$LedgerPath = '',
  [string]$Gate = ''
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'

if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($RepoRoot)) {
  $RepoRoot = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
}
if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($RegistryPath)) {
  $RegistryPath = Join-Path $RepoRoot 'state\standards\gate-advisory-registry.json'
}

$counts = @{ allow = 0; verdict_warn = 0; infra_warn = 0 }
$events = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]

function Get-AdvisoryUtcNow { return [DateTime]::UtcNow.ToString('o') }

function Add-AdvisoryEvent {
  param([string]$Name, [string]$Channel, [int]$ExitCode, [string]$Detail)
  $counts[$Channel]++
  $events.Add([ordered]@{
    at = Get-AdvisoryUtcNow
    source = 'run-advisory-gates'
    gate = $Name
    channel = $Channel
    exit = $ExitCode
    detail = $Detail
  }) | Out-Null
  if ($Channel -eq 'allow') {
    Write-Output "GATE_ADVISORY[$Name] channel=allow exit=$ExitCode"
  } else {
    Write-Output "GATE_ADVISORY[$Name] channel=$Channel exit=$ExitCode $Detail"
    Write-Warning "GATE_WARN[$Name] $Channel (advisory: not blocking) $Detail"
  }
}

function Invoke-AdvisoryScript {
  param([string]$ScriptPath, [string[]]$ScriptArgs)
  $prior = Get-Location
  try {
    Set-Location -LiteralPath $RepoRoot
    & pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $ScriptPath @ScriptArgs *>&1 | Out-Null
    $code = $LASTEXITCODE
    if ($null -eq $code) { $code = 126 }
    return [int]$code
  } catch {
    return 127
  } finally {
    Set-Location -LiteralPath $prior
  }
}

$registry = $null
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $RegistryPath -PathType Leaf) {
  try { $registry = Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath $RegistryPath -Encoding utf8 | ConvertFrom-Json }
  catch { $registry = $null }
}
if ($null -eq $registry) {
  Write-Warning "REGISTRY_UNREADABLE $RegistryPath (advisory: proceeding)"
  Write-Output "ADVISORY_GATES_SUMMARY gates=0 allow=0 verdict_warn=0 infra_warn=1 exit=0 (advisory: never blocks)"
  exit 0
}

if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($LedgerPath)) {
  $LedgerPath = Join-Path $RepoRoot ([string]$registry.ledger_path -replace '/', '\')
}

$gates = @($registry.gates)
if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Gate)) {
  $gates = @($gates | Where-Object { [string]$_.name -eq $Gate })
}

foreach ($entry in $gates) {
  $name = [string]$entry.name
  $scriptRel = [string]$entry.script
  $scriptPath = Join-Path $RepoRoot ($scriptRel -replace '/', '\')
  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $scriptPath -PathType Leaf)) {
    Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'infra_warn' -ExitCode 127 -Detail "script_missing:$scriptRel"
    continue
  }

  $hasDocGlob = $false
  if ($entry.PSObject.Properties['doc_glob'] -and -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$entry.doc_glob)) {
    $hasDocGlob = $true
  }

  if ($hasDocGlob) {
    # Per-document mode: run once per doc containing doc_marker; zero declaring docs = vacuous allow.
    $globRoot = Join-Path $RepoRoot (([string]$entry.doc_glob -split '/')[0])
    $marker = [string]$entry.doc_marker
    $docs = @()
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $globRoot -PathType Container) {
      $docs = @(Get-ChildItem -Path $globRoot -Recurse -Filter '*.md' -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object { (Select-String -LiteralPath $_.FullName -Pattern $marker -SimpleMatch -Quiet -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) })
    }
    if (@($docs).Count -eq 0) {
      Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'allow' -ExitCode 0 -Detail 'vacuous_allow:no_declaring_docs'
      continue
    }
    $worst = 0
    $failedDoc = ''
    foreach ($doc in $docs) {
      $args = @()
      foreach ($a in @($entry.args)) {
        $args += (([string]$a) -replace '\{doc\}', $doc.FullName) -replace '\{repoRoot\}', $RepoRoot
      }
      $code = Invoke-AdvisoryScript -ScriptPath $scriptPath -ScriptArgs $args
      if ($code -ne 0 -and $worst -eq 0) { $worst = $code; $failedDoc = $doc.FullName }
    }
    if ($worst -eq 0) {
      Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'allow' -ExitCode 0 -Detail ("docs=" + @($docs).Count)
    } else {
      Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'verdict_warn' -ExitCode $worst -Detail "doc=$failedDoc"
    }
    continue
  }

  $args = @()
  foreach ($a in @($entry.args)) { $args += ([string]$a -replace '\{repoRoot\}', $RepoRoot) }
  $code = Invoke-AdvisoryScript -ScriptPath $scriptPath -ScriptArgs $args
  if ($code -eq 0) {
    Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'allow' -ExitCode 0 -Detail ''
  } elseif ($code -ge 126) {
    Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'infra_warn' -ExitCode $code -Detail 'script_crash_or_unlaunchable'
  } else {
    Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'verdict_warn' -ExitCode $code -Detail ''
  }
}

# Best-effort ledger append (utf8 no BOM, one JSON object per line); failure is only a warning.
try {
  $ledgerDir = Split-Path -Parent $LedgerPath
  if ($ledgerDir -and -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $ledgerDir -PathType Container)) {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $ledgerDir -Force | Out-Null
  }
  $sb = New-Object System.Text.StringBuilder
  foreach ($e in $events) { [void]$sb.AppendLine(($e | ConvertTo-Json -Compress -Depth 6)) }
  [IO.File]::AppendAllText($LedgerPath, $sb.ToString().Replace("`r`n", "`n"), [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))
} catch {
  Write-Warning "LEDGER_APPEND_FAILED $LedgerPath (advisory: proceeding)"
}

Write-Output ("ADVISORY_GATES_SUMMARY gates=" + @($gates).Count + " allow=" + $counts.allow + " verdict_warn=" + $counts.verdict_warn + " infra_warn=" + $counts.infra_warn + " exit=0 (advisory: never blocks)")
exit 0

  try {
    Set-Location -LiteralPath $RepoRoot
    & pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $ScriptPath @ScriptArgs *>&1 | Out-Null
    $code = $LASTEXITCODE
    if ($null -eq $code) { $code = 126 }
    return [int]$code
  } catch {
    return 127
  } finally {
    Set-Location -LiteralPath $prior
  }
}

$registry = $null
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $RegistryPath -PathType Leaf) {
  try { $registry = Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath $RegistryPath -Encoding utf8 | ConvertFrom-Json }
  catch { $registry = $null }
}
if ($null -eq $registry) {
  Write-Warning "REGISTRY_UNREADABLE $RegistryPath (advisory: proceeding)"
  Write-Output "ADVISORY_GATES_SUMMARY gates=0 allow=0 verdict_warn=0 infra_warn=1 exit=0 (advisory: never blocks)"
  exit 0
}

}

$gates = @($registry.gates)
if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Gate)) {
  $gates = @($gates | Where-Object { [string]$_.name -eq $Gate })
}

foreach ($entry in $gates) {
  $name = [string]$entry.name
  $scriptRel = [string]$entry.script
  $scriptPath = Join-Path $RepoRoot ($scriptRel -replace '/', '\')
  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $scriptPath -PathType Leaf)) {
    Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'infra_warn' -ExitCode 127 -Detail "script_missing:$scriptRel"
    continue
  }

  $hasDocGlob = $false
  if ($entry.PSObject.Properties['doc_glob'] -and -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$entry.doc_glob)) {
    $hasDocGlob = $true
  }

  if ($hasDocGlob) {
    # Per-document mode: run once per doc containing doc_marker; zero declaring docs = vacuous allow.
    $globRoot = Join-Path $RepoRoot (([string]$entry.doc_glob -split '/')[0])
    $marker = [string]$entry.doc_marker
    $docs = @()
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $globRoot -PathType Container) {
      $docs = @(Get-ChildItem -Path $globRoot -Recurse -Filter '*.md' -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object { (Select-String -LiteralPath $_.FullName -Pattern $marker -SimpleMatch -Quiet -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) })
    }
    if (@($docs).Count -eq 0) {
      Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'allow' -ExitCode 0 -Detail 'vacuous_allow:no_declaring_docs'
      continue
    }
    $worst = 0
    $failedDoc = ''
    foreach ($doc in $docs) {
      $args = @()
      foreach ($a in @($entry.args)) {
        $args += (([string]$a) -replace '\{doc\}', $doc.FullName) -replace '\{repoRoot\}', $RepoRoot
      }
      $code = Invoke-AdvisoryScript -ScriptPath $scriptPath -ScriptArgs $args
      if ($code -ne 0 -and $worst -eq 0) { $worst = $code; $failedDoc = $doc.FullName }
    }
    if ($worst -eq 0) {
      Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'allow' -ExitCode 0 -Detail ("docs=" + @($docs).Count)
    } else {
      Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'verdict_warn' -ExitCode $worst -Detail "doc=$failedDoc"
    }
    continue
  }

  $args = @()
  foreach ($a in @($entry.args)) { $args += ([string]$a -replace '\{repoRoot\}', $RepoRoot) }
  $code = Invoke-AdvisoryScript -ScriptPath $scriptPath -ScriptArgs $args
  if ($code -eq 0) {
    Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'allow' -ExitCode 0 -Detail ''
  } elseif ($code -ge 126) {
    Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'infra_warn' -ExitCode $code -Detail 'script_crash_or_unlaunchable'
  } else {
    Add-AdvisoryEvent -Name $name -Channel 'verdict_warn' -ExitCode $code -Detail ''
  }

  $ledgerDir = Split-Path -Parent $LedgerPath
  if ($ledgerDir -and -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $ledgerDir -PathType Container)) {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $ledgerDir -Force | Out-Null
  }
  $sb = New-Object System.Text.StringBuilder
  foreach ($e in $events) { [void]$sb.AppendLine(($e | ConvertTo-Json -Compress -Depth 6)) }
  [IO.File]::AppendAllText($LedgerPath, $sb.ToString().Replace("`r`n", "`n"), [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))
} catch {
  Write-Warning "LEDGER_APPEND_FAILED $LedgerPath (advisory: proceeding)"
}

Talent WC-209 passed code review with three P2-level issues that are refinements rather than blockers—things like adding a skipped-row counter with a threshold and adjusting max duration. The reviewer confirmed all the critical security and reliability aspects are solid: SSRF protection on both hops, fail-honest error handling, idempotency via database constraints, proper scope isolation, and integration with existing downstream systems using real test fixtures. The P2s are small enough to close out now.

For the first two fixes, I'm modifying the parser to count skipped rows and have the monitor persist that count in the run record, marking the run as failed or partial if it exceeds a threshold. This touches the listing module to return the skipped count, the monitor to persist and check it, and likely the database migration—either adding a new column to the runs table or storing the count in an existing JSON field like error_detail to avoid a schema change. Since the migration hasn't shipped yet, I can amend it freely to add a skipped_rows column. The logic is straightforward: if skipped rows exist and the ratio exceeds 50% or there are no entries at all, mark the run failed; otherwise keep it as ok but record the skipped count.

For the second fix, I'm adding a Vercel max duration constant to the cron route to allow up to 300 seconds on the pro plan. After that, I'll rerun the tests, update the AR evidence, and merge.

"""Cross-document comparison API endpoint — POST /comparison/derive.

Thin read-path wrapper over the deterministic
``cross_document_comparison.compute_cross_document_derived_fact`` subordinate
service. Computes a cross-document derived fact from two caller-supplied
``Fact`` records and returns the deterministic ``DerivedFact`` plus a trace
verification result.

This route is stateless and read-only: it neither mutates the active pack nor
creates a side truth path. Every derived fact still flows through the standard
citation/derived-fact kernel gates when consumed downstream. No LLM is on this
path — the comparison core stays deterministic by design.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from api._limiter import limiter
from veridyn.cross_document_comparison import (
    compute_cross_document_derived_fact,
    verify_cross_document_trace,
)
from veridyn.exceptions import PrecisionError
from veridyn.types import Fact

router = APIRouter(tags=["comparison"])


def _require_op(request: Request) -> None:
    from api.routes.admin_auth import _require_admin_permission
    _require_admin_permission(request, "admin:manage_rules")


class FactInput(BaseModel):
    """Caller-supplied fact record. Mirrors the subset of ``Fact`` needed for
    deterministic cross-document comparison. Validated by reconstructing a
    ``Fact`` domain model, so source_truth / value invariants are enforced."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    fact_id: str
    fact_key: str
    value: Any
    value_type: str
    source_kind: str = "user_input"
    source_document_id: str | None = None
    source_span_id: str | None = None
    extraction_method: str = "manual"
    status: str = "accepted"
    confidence: str = "1.0"


class ComparisonDeriveRequest(BaseModel):
    left_fact: FactInput
    right_fact: FactInput
    operator: str = Field(..., description="One of: ==, !=, >, >=, <, <=")
    derived_fact_key: str
    comparison_parameters: dict[str, Any] | None = None


def _to_fact(raw: FactInput) -> Fact:
    """Reconstruct a validated ``Fact`` domain object from the request shape.

    ``Fact.value`` rejects floats; Pydantic will surface that as a 422. The
    request model accepts ``Any`` so the domain validator owns the rules.
    """
    return Fact(
        fact_id=raw.fact_id,
        fact_key=raw.fact_key,
        value=raw.value,
        value_type=raw.value_type,
        source_kind=raw.source_kind,
        source_document_id=raw.source_document_id,
        source_span_id=raw.source_span_id,
        extraction_method=raw.extraction_method,
        status=raw.status,
        confidence=raw.confidence,
    )


@router.post("/comparison/derive")
@limiter.limit("60/minute")
async def derive_cross_document_fact(
    request: Request,
    body: ComparisonDeriveRequest,
    _op: None = Depends(_require_op),
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Compute a deterministic cross-document derived fact.

    Returns the derived fact with its comparison trace and an independent
    verification of that trace. No session, active-pack, or ledger mutation
    occurs — this is a pure read-path over two caller-supplied facts.
    """
    try:
        left_fact = _to_fact(body.left_fact)
        right_fact = _to_fact(body.right_fact)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=422,
            detail={"status": "invalid_fact", "error": str(exc)},
        ) from exc

    try:
        derived = compute_cross_document_derived_fact(
            left_fact=left_fact,
            right_fact=right_fact,
            operator=body.operator,
            derived_fact_key=body.derived_fact_key,
            comparison_parameters=body.comparison_parameters,
        )
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=422,
            detail={"status": "unsupported_operator", "error": str(exc)},
        ) from exc
    except PrecisionError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=422,
            detail={"status": "precision_error", "error": str(exc)},
        ) from exc

    trace_valid, trace_errors = verify_cross_document_trace(derived)
    return {
        "status": "derived",
        "derived_fact": derived.model_dump(mode="json"),
        "trace_verification": {
            "valid": trace_valid,
            "errors": trace_errors,
        },
    }

/**
 * PI-OB-P2 — the PRODUCER half of the product-intelligence live surface.
 *
 * The 249-line `readLiveProductSource` boundary (live-source-boundary.ts) is the
 * real consumer: it reads `<portfolio-core state root>/product-intelligence/<product_id>/card.json`.
 * Until now NOTHING produced that card, so every real caller got MISSING_POINTER.
 * This module is the missing producer: it emits operatorbench's OWN real
 * product-intelligence card to exactly the pointer the boundary reads, so the
 * live page renders the honest CANNOT_EVALUATE read (real provenance) instead of
 * the MISSING_POINTER error card.

 * load-bearing fields are exactly what the boundary's CROSS_PRODUCT check and the
 * live-workspace VERSION_MISMATCH check require; everything else is honest metadata.
 *
 * Bounded write: the emitter creates ONLY `<root>/product-intelligence/<product_id>/`

content.text:
The portfolio-state cards are stale (all showing mid-June deploys), but that itself is a finding: **the whole fleet is weeks behind main** — nothing merged this session, or for weeks prior, is live. Here's the honest build-to-finish inventory.

## Executive summary
- **"Finish" = the FABLE program**, not wire-or-cut: build every cell to full → deploy it → prove it live → make it recoverable. That's multi-week, and the true blockers are operator-gated (money/regulated/credentials), not code.
- **Net-new build** is dominated by two products: **aurasphere** (whole product to live) and **Agentic's 5 v2 backends** (real engines, zero frontends).
- **Currency is the cheapest big win**: ~10 products need redeploy-to-HEAD; the code is merged, just not live.
- **Nothing is restore-tested** — the entire DR/recovery ladder is unbuilt.
- **The mco "backend company" loop** (detect→alert→fix→verify) is ~40% wired.
- Money/regulated activations (bd-pay, aurasphere deploy, credentials) are **yours to authorize** — agents build up to the gate, not through it.

## Tier 1 — Net-new BUILD (the actual "building")
| Product | What's left to build | Size |
|---|---|---|
| **aurasphere** | Serve 42 real routes (only 1/43 deployed), wire 11 orphan gateway clients to pages, light 7 dark packages | **Large** |
| **Agentic** | 5 v2 consumer stacks — commercial/effects/plans/connectors/real-client backends exist, **no UI** | **Large** |
| **bd-pay** | Disputes FSM + approval-requests + real auth/session; cut 2 phantoms *(ERT-gated — money)* | Med-careful |
| **veridyn** | Activate the merged/compiled-pack load lane (WC-210 task-1) | Small |
| **protein** | Multitenant addon (tenant-scope every mutating route); real integrations when consumers exist | Medium |
| **portfolio-core** | Adopt conformance/capability-manifest/product-model; better-version showdown on outbox/durable-workflow/federation-snapshot | Medium |
| Khep · Talent · DataRoom · DSE | FABLE per-cell deltas: Khep trust/safety+KYC; Talent PII-at-rest+object-storage+audit; DataRoom legal pack+export+CI scans; DSE idempotency+float-proof | Medium each |

## Tier 2 — Make it LIVE (currency — cheapest, highest visibility)
Every product is drifted. **Redeploy-to-HEAD across ~10 products** — most are config-only, but **talent needs a money-column DB migration** (15 days behind, verified) and **dse/bd-pay/mco/aurasphere/veridyn-compliance have no deploy at all**. This is where all merged work actually goes live.

## Tier 3 — Make it PROVABLE + RECOVERABLE (the bulk of "done")
- **17 golden journeys** — one authenticated, reconciled, continuously-probed user path per product → the LIVE_PROVEN bar.
- **DR ladder (unbuilt)**: escrow bundles, credential vault repair, off-host backups, **restore drills per product**, clean-room estate drill. Nothing is `RESTORE_TESTED` today.
- **mco backend loop**: finish detect→incident→alert→fix→verify (WC-401–404) so the estate runs itself.
- **Provenance**: `/provenance` + live `/migration` on all products; release objects.

## Operator-gated (agents can't finish these)
bd-pay live money (BB/BFIU/sponsor/HSM) · aurasphere live regulated deploy · WC-503 credential provisioning + vault · DSE live-money promotion. Agents build to the gate; you flip it.

## Bottom line
The **critical path** to a done estate: (1) fleet redeploy + DR foundation → (2) provenance + one golden journey per product → (3) the big builds (aurasphere, Agentic consumers, bd-pay disputes) → (4) restore drills → certification. Agents can drive most of 1–3; roughly **a few focused weeks of dispatch**, gated at the end by the money/regulated/credential items only you can authorize.

Want me to start the cheapest-highest-value tier now — the fleet redeploy sweep — or open the aurasphere and Agentic build lanes?

Every miss was the same: I answered "what's built / deployed / live" from artifacts already in my context — planning specs, 43h-stale state cards, earlier tool output — instead of **probing live truth at the moment of the claim**.

## The rule (now encoded, in effect next session)
**No claim about build/deploy/live state ships as fact without a live probe at claim-time** — the product's `/api/health` (deployed_sha), the feature-gate config (`features.ts`/`*_MODE`), or `anchor-probe`. Can't probe → the claim is labeled *"unverified / from plan,"* never stated as truth.

## Why the rule isn't enough by itself — 3 mechanical backstops
Behavior is the weak link (I ignored the "STALE 43h" banner that fired correctly every session). So don't rely on my discipline — make the system refuse stale-sourced claims:

| Fix | What it stops | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Freshness gate** — `block_if_not_current` auto-runs `anchor-probe` and refuses to serve a card past its SLA | Citing mid-June cards as "current" (miss #3) | S — highest leverage |

| **3. Provenance labels on plan docs** — a spec figure ("17 journeys") can't substitute for measured state | Quoting the plan as truth (miss #1) | S |

Backstop #1 alone would have caught all three, because every error traced to trusting a stale artifact over a fresh probe.

## The behavioral discipline that *did* work — extend it
The **adjudication** held up — real tools, keep-on-doubt, adversarial cross-family AR. The cuts were safe. I dropped that same discipline for *conversational state answers*. The fix is symmetric: **run the "refute my own claim" pass on state answers too**, not just on code changes. A state claim with no live probe is `CANNOT_EVALUATE`, never a `PASS` — same standard as everything else.

Durable rule: done. The real prevention is backstop #1 — a freshness gate that makes it *impossible* to cite a stale card as live. Want me to build it? #!/usr/bin/env npx tsx
/**

## Adversarial Review — portfolio-core freshness gate (context-engine)

**Scope:** SHARED INFRA (context-engine MCP server, every session's SessionStart + agent context tools depend on it). Reviewed the staged diff: `engine.ts`, `gates.ts`, `mcp-server.ts`, `types.ts`, `current-truth-render.test.ts`.

### Verification results

| # | Claim | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `summarizeProbeFreshness` correctness | ✅ `is_stale = probe older than SLA (via `record.standard.qualityBarProfile` → `QUALITY_BAR_PROFILES[...].freshness_sla_minutes`) OR probe absent`; `sha_drift` logic present; `required_action` names `anchor-probe` when stale, `null` when fresh |
| 2 | No-throw / no regression on partial record | ✅ Optional chaining throughout (`record.standard?.`, `probe?.`); `DEFAULT_FRESHNESS_SLA_MINUTES = 120` fallback; pre-existing fixture (no `standard`, no `live_probe`) covered. `current-truth-render.test.ts` → **5/5 pass** |
| 3 | Envelope is unmissable | ✅ `freshness` is the **first** key in `renderCurrentTruth` output (`engine.ts:1313`); `blockIfNotCurrent` result includes `freshness` (`gates.ts:832`) |
| 4 | Opt-in refresh safety | ✅ (a) default path unchanged (only fires on `refresh:true`); (b) all failures caught → `{ok:false}`; (c) 90s `timeout`; (d) `/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/i` regex guard **before** `shell:true` execFileSync |
| 5 | Types | ✅ `FreshnessSummary` in `types.ts:316`, imported by `engine.ts`; `ClaimPreflightResult.freshness?` optional. `tsc -p context-engine/tsconfig.json --noEmit` → **EXIT 0** |
| 6 | Pre-existing flake | ✅ **Independently confirmed**: (a) `registry-awareness.test.ts` alone → **27/27 pass** on feature branch; (b) staged diff grep for `task-pack`/`loadTaskPacks`/`registry-awareness`/`checkDuplicateWork` → **zero matches**; (c) reproduced the **identical ENOENT-on-task-pack** failure on a clean `origin/main` baseline worktree (same `loadTaskPacks`→`checkDuplicateWork` path, same `AppData\Local\portfolio-core\context-runtime\task-packs\` directory). It is environment-state, not this diff. |

---

DEFECTS: none

BOTTLENECKS: none

IMPROVEMENTS:
1. **P2 — `sha_drift` is stricter than the brief's literal spec (intentional, document it).** Brief said `sha_drift = deploy_sha != origin_main_sha`; implementation is `Boolean(deploySha && originMainSha && deploySha !== originMainSha)`. This is the *more correct* reading (can't claim drift without both shas) and is consistent with `deploy_state_unverified` already being true when stale — but a one-line comment in `engine.ts:322` stating "drift requires both shas present" would prevent a future reader from "fixing" it toward the literal spec and introducing false drift when one sha is null.
2. **P2 — `tryReanchorProduct` lives above the `gates` import block (`mcp-server.ts:1-34`).** Stylistic only; functions are hoisted, no behavior impact. Moving it below the imports (or into its own module) would read cleaner since it's the only non-import top-level code in the file header.
3. **P3 — Refresh response shape diverges from non-refresh response.** When `refresh:true` and stale, the result is `{ refresh_attempted, ...renderCurrentTruth(record) }`; the non-refresh path returns `renderCurrentTruth(record)` bare. The `freshness` envelope is still top-level in both (spread last), so callers reading `is_stale` are unaffected — but a consumer diffing the two shapes will see an extra key. Acceptable for an opt-in debug affordance; worth a one-line note in the tool description if it stabilizes.
4. **P3 — Brief undercounted the flake.** Brief said "ONE failure"; the feature-branch full run showed **two** (both registry-awareness, identical ENOENT root cause), and the origin/main baseline showed **one** (snapshot.test.ts, same root cause). The count is non-deterministic (test-ordering/parallelism race on shared AppData task-pack files). Not a defect in this diff — but the brief's "ONE failure" framing should be corrected to "a flaky, count-varying ENOENT-on-task-pack failure" in any closeout note, so a future reviewer doesn't think the count drifted due to this change.

VERDICT: PASS

content.content:
The edge no longer hand-reimplements `/v1/doctors` and a 404 fallback. `handle()` now:
1. **Infrastructure probes stay exactly as-is** (`/api/health`, `/healthz`, `/readyz`) — never delegated, so a dark feature can't take down liveness/readiness.
2. **Body cap** — enforced at the edge before any route translation. For the `EdgeRequest` direct path, `checkBodySize` rejects a serialized body over `MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES` (413). For the deployable HTTP server, `readJsonBody` enforces it at the **stream level** (stops buffering past the cap, drains the rest so the client gets a clean 413, never an `ECONNRESET`).
3. **`matchRoute`** → unknown route returns the house 404.
4. **`translateRouteContext`** — a single `handlerStub`-keyed switch translates the HTTP request into the composition root's typed ctx: GET routes consume query strings (`doctorQuery`, `slotsQuery`, `complianceQuery`, `auditQuery`, `analyticsQuery`); POST/PUT/PATCH routes forward the parsed JSON body (`authBody`, `paymentIntent`, `bookingBody`, `recordBody`, `consentBody`, …). The ctx body interfaces all carry `[k: string]: unknown`, so server-authoritative fields (patient_id, fee, geometry, principal) stay token/server-derived inside the handler — the edge grants no authority it doesn't have.
5. **`composed.gateway.handle`** runs the full pipeline (gate → auth → residency → rate-limit → dispatch) and the edge returns its `GatewayResponse` verbatim.

### Gate is the switch (counts)
`/api/health` `route_reachability` is now **derived from the live feature posture**, not a hardcoded whitelist:
- **canonical_route_count: 43**
- **served_when_active: 39** (core spine + the 4 regulated gates that are `active` in the default posture)
- **gated_off_by_default: 4** — `GET /v1/analytics/{provider,operator,clinic}` (gated by `practice_analytics`, quality) and `POST /v1/admin/payout-batches/{id}/release` (gated by `payments_bd_pay_live`, bd_pay_activation)

A dark_built/suspended feature returns the composition's own house 404-gated response (`{code:"not_found", message:'feature "X" is not available'}`) — never short-circuited, never a 500/stack trace.

### The button proof (test result)
`THE BUTTON` test passes: with the **default** posture, `GET /v1/analytics/provider` → **404 gated**; with a **config-only** posture flipping `practice_analytics` → `active` (same code path, `postureFlipping()` helper), the same route → **serves** (handler runs, not the gated 404); flipped **back to dark_built** → gates again. A companion test proves the `/api/health` reachability counts move with the same flip (route leaves `gated_off_by_default_routes`, joins `served_when_active_routes`). **No `FeatureGate` default state was changed** — regulated gates stay dark_built/suspended.

### Files changed (staged, not committed)
- `services/api/src/edge.ts` — delegation loop, `readJsonBody`/`checkBodySize`, `translateRouteContext`, gate-derived `resolveRouteReachability`, threaded `FeatureGateRegistry`.
- `services/api/src/composition.ts` — `export const ROUTE_FEATURE` (single source of truth for reachability).
- `services/api/test/edge.test.ts` — relaxed `/api/health` assertion to the derived model; added 7 tests (active-route delegation ×2, dark_built gated response, the button flip + reachability reflection, body cap on direct path + HTTP stream path, HTTP POST body decode).

### Test summary
- **tsc (`-p tsconfig.json --noEmit` + web typecheck): clean**
- **`npm test` (test:json + test:gate): 1803/1803 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip** (was 1801; +2 net new edge tests)
- **edge.test.ts: 22/22 pass** (15 existing preserved + 7 new)
- **integrity gate: 6/6 pass** against the real JSON report

No deployment performed. `git add` done; no commit (per brief).

M  services/api/src/edge.ts
M  services/api/test/edge.test.ts

The dispatch resolves the booking via `assertOwnBooking` but **discards `idor.value`**, forwarding the client `ctx.paymentIntent` unchanged to `createIntent` (composition.ts:543), which validates only integer-paisa *format* via `paisa()` and never reconciles `amount_paisa` against the booking's server-authoritative `fee_paisa`. `payments_pay_at_clinic` is **active by default** (contracts/src/features.ts:84), so the route serves today: an authenticated patient creates a payment-intent record for their *own* booking (IDOR check passes) at an **arbitrary amount**, persisted to the intent store; the MDR split (bd-pay/mdr.ts) computes off that amount. Fix: in the dispatch, set/validate `amount_paisa` from `idor.value.fee_paisa` before `createIntent`. content.thinking:
The security audit found a critical vulnerability in the payment system — by exposing the `POST /v1/payments/intent` endpoint through edge delegation, it revealed a pre-existing IDOR flaw where the payment intent dispatch can be manipulated through the booking ownership check, which is exactly the kind of defect that matters when handling financial transactions.

The core issue is that while the endpoint validates the patient owns the booking, it discards the authorization context and forwards the client-supplied amount directly to payment intent creation without reconciling it against the server's authoritative booking fee. This means an authenticated patient can create a payment intent for their own booking at any arbitrary amount. The defect is rated P1 because while it's currently a data-integrity issue (the payment rails are disabled by default), flipping the `payments_bd_pay_live` config flag would make this exploitable for actual money theft — and that's a configuration-only change with no code review gate, which is the real danger here.

The fix is straightforward: derive and validate the `amount_paisa` from the booking's `fee_paisa` server-side before calling `createIntent`, ensuring the amount always comes from the server, never the client. 58	## 2. Doctrine and definitions
59	
60	- **WIRED** — reachable on the real path (deployed or on the canonical launch path), not behind a dead seam/env-off default.
61	- **USED** — has ≥1 named consumer with evidence: source caller, cron, plugin, external product, or human workflow with artifacts.
62	- **PHANTOM** — a client calls an endpoint that does not exist (bd-pay apps), or a doc claims a module that does not exist (dse `dse_engine.api`).
63	- **DEAD** — no consumer and no scheduled wiring PR. Disposition: archive/delete.
64	- **OVERCLAIM** — naming/marketing implies live capability the code does not have (dataroom "verification" chips; BishomIQ enterprise "Live"; "completion verifier" in Khep).
65	- **THE LAW (consumer-first):** from ratification, no PR merges a new package, spec, gate, scheduler job, endpoint, or UI surface **without its consumer wired in the same PR** (or a named consumer + dated wiring ticket in the PR body). Contracts freeze only at ≥2 real product importers. Campaign status documents must be generated from git queries, never hand-written (falsifier: the SAAD-17 ledger was 4 days wrong about its own central blocker, #442 vs merged #467).

71	## 2A. FABLE-GRADE QUALITY BAR (binding on every work package)
72	
73	**Definition — Fable-grade:** a product is Fable-grade when a skeptical senior engineer, given only the live URL and the repo, can verify within one hour that every advertised feature works end-to-end on the **deployed** surface; that nothing advertised is mock, fixture, phantom, or partial; and that every quality floor below is met with fresh evidence. It reads as if built from the ground up in one coherent pass: no dead code, no stale docs, no unlabeled mocks, no scars.
74	
75	**Every WC in this spec inherits ALL floors below. A floor without evidence is a failed floor. There is no partial credit anywhere in this section.**

107	### Anti-compromise enforcement (how this spec makes partial work impossible)
108	
109	- **E-1 Binary completion.** A WC or feature is DONE only when **every** acceptance criterion and **every** QM floor has attached evidence. "90% done" does not exist in this program: the registry status is `done` or it is not, and `done` without the full evidence bundle is a falsified record (P0 defect against the agent's work, treated the same as a failing test).
110	- **E-2 No partial merges.** An agent MUST NOT merge a subset of a work package and defer the remainder. Follow-up promises in PR text are void — gates treat them as non-existent. The only legitimate way to reduce scope is an operator waiver recorded in the task registry (`waivers[]`: id, date, exact scope, reason). No waiver in the registry = full scope binds.
111	- **E-3 Banned claim language.** PR bodies, status entries, and closure comments may not contain: "mostly done", "should work", "works locally", "will be wired later", "temporarily mocked", "left as follow-up", "good enough for now", or TODO/FIXME in shipped paths. CI grep rejects the merge.
112	- **E-4 Evidence contract.** Every closure MUST attach, in the PR or closure comment: (a) commands run with exit codes; (b) live probe output — URL, `deployed_sha`, timestamp; (c) test summary in the exact form `total/pass/fail/skip = N/N/0/0`; (d) video or trace for any UI change; (e) the filled QM checklist (all 8 floors, each with a pointer to its evidence). Any missing item = not closed, regardless of how convincing the prose is.
113	- **E-5 Scope frozen at dispatch.** Agents may not narrow scope, swap acceptance criteria, or reinterpret "consumer" mid-task. If genuinely blocked, the correct and **rewarded** outcome is to STOP and record the blocker in the registry with evidence. A recorded blocker is a successful result; a silent partial merge is a failed one.
114	- **E-6 Mock and fixture rules.** Mocks live only in tests and explicitly labeled dev modes. Any shipped surface backed by fixture data must render a visible label (ModeChip / "EXPERIMENT"). An unlabeled fixture on a shipped surface is a P0 defect.
115	- **E-7 Green tests ≠ done.** The veridyn-bootstrap proof policy binds portfolio-wide: closure requires runtime proof on the supported launch path **plus** real user-path proof for the claimed surface. Tests are regression signals, never readiness proof. Claims without runtime evidence are `NOT PROVEN`, and `NOT PROVEN` cannot close a WC.
116	- **E-8 Adversarial review.** Every WC closure receives an AR (DEFECTS bucket decides) from a **different model family** than the builder. PASS required; PUSHBACK/FAIL loops back to the builder. The reviewer must independently re-run at least the live probe and the test summary — reviewer sign-off without re-execution is itself a DEFECT.
117	- **E-9 One-hour verification test.** Before closing a Phase-2 product WC, the closing agent must perform (and attach) the Fable-grade check itself: starting from only the live URL and repo, verify every advertised feature end-to-end within one hour and record the walkthrough. If the agent cannot, the product is not at bar — no exceptions.
